title: Reset Synchronizer
constraints: `arst_n` is an asynchronous, active-low reset from a pin. `rst_n` is the reset for the logic in the `clk` domain.
**Assertion is asynchronous:** when `arst_n` falls, `rst_n` falls immediately, even if `clk` is stopped.
**Deassertion is synchronous:** after `arst_n` rises, `rst_n` rises exactly at the **second** rising edge of `clk`, so every flop leaves reset in the same cycle.
Use two flip-flops. Must be synthesizable.
hints: Two flops with asynchronous clear from `arst_n`. The first samples a constant 1.
`always @(posedge clk or negedge arst_n) if (!arst_n) s <= 2'b00; else s <= {s[0], 1'b1};`
Why not a plain synchronous reset? It can't reset the logic while the clock is stopped, and a purely asynchronous release can violate recovery/removal timing and leave flops metastable.

examples.check: deasserts on the second rising edge
examples.title: release
examples.expected: rst_n rises at the 2nd following clk edge

examples.title: glitch
examples.input: a 1 ns low pulse on arst_n
